title: Confidentiality versus serious preventable harm to a third party
short_description: During outpatient treatment, a patient tells a mental-health clinician about a concrete plan to seriously injure an identifiable former partner, has access to the means described, and refuses voluntary warning or safety planning.
decision_question: When a patient presents a serious, credible threat to an identifiable person, what confidentiality rule should govern targeted disclosure intended to reduce that risk?
position_families: Maintain confidentiality unless a still higher/imminent threshold is met, while intensifying treatment and voluntary safety planning
Make minimum-necessary targeted disclosure once serious harm to an identifiable person is reasonably probable and voluntary mitigation is insufficient
Use a stepped duty-to-protect policy that first seeks patient-mediated or clinical containment and escalates to targeted disclosure when those measures cannot adequately reduce risk
Broader protective-action approaches involving law enforcement or emergency intervention when the specified threshold is met

scenario: During outpatient treatment, a patient describes a specific plan to seriously injure an identifiable former partner, identifies when the confrontation is intended to occur, and has access to the means described. The clinician conducts a structured risk assessment and, based on the specificity, means and recent escalation, judges serious physical harm to the former partner reasonably probable rather than merely possible. The patient refuses to contact the person, involve a trusted supporter or participate in another voluntary safety plan. A limited disclosure to the intended person and/or an appropriate protective service could materially reduce risk, but broader disclosure could damage privacy and the therapeutic relationship. For this benchmark, assume disclosure is legally permitted but not automatically required and that the clinician may choose among the represented policies. The service must decide what confidentiality rule and disclosure threshold should apply.
